description: RTOS internals decomposed. Task control blocks, ready queues, context switching, IPC primitives (queue, semaphore, mutex, event group), tickless idle, FreeRTOS specifics. The mechanisms by which a few KB of code provides preemptive multitasking on tiny MCUs.

sub_mechanisms.name: task_control_block
sub_mechanisms.definition: TCB: per-task data structure. Stack pointer, priority, state, registers (on context switch), wait reason.
sub_mechanisms.why: Heart of RTOS. Each task is a TCB + stack. Scheduler manages list of TCBs. Compact (few hundred bytes).

sub_mechanisms.name: ready_queue_per_priority
sub_mechanisms.definition: FreeRTOS: array of lists, indexed by priority. Bitmask of which priorities have ready tasks.
sub_mechanisms.why: O(1) highest-priority task selection. Bitmask + count-leading-zeros instruction = fast scheduler. Cortex-M has CLZ.

sub_mechanisms.name: context_switch_RT
sub_mechanisms.definition: Save current task registers to its stack; restore next task's registers from its stack; jump to next task's PC.
sub_mechanisms.why: Inversely proportional to context switch overhead = how short critical sections can be. Cortex-M PendSV handler typical implementation.

sub_mechanisms.name: PendSV_context_switch
sub_mechanisms.definition: Cortex-M PendSV exception. Software-triggered, lowest priority. Used for RTOS context switches.
sub_mechanisms.why: RTOS triggers PendSV from higher-priority context; PendSV fires when no interrupts pending. Clean context switch mechanism.

sub_mechanisms.name: FreeRTOS_queue
sub_mechanisms.definition: FIFO + circular buffer. Thread-safe push/pop. Blocking with timeout.
sub_mechanisms.why: Primary IPC. Task → ISR communication. xQueueSendFromISR variants for interrupt context. Foundation of FreeRTOS designs.

sub_mechanisms.name: FreeRTOS_semaphore
sub_mechanisms.definition: Binary or counting. Acquire/release. Block on empty acquire.
sub_mechanisms.why: Resource pool counting (counting), simple signal (binary). Often replaced by direct task notifications for performance.

sub_mechanisms.name: FreeRTOS_mutex_priority_inheritance
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mutex with priority inheritance. Owner-tracked. Recursive mutex variant.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard for protecting shared resources. Inheritance bounds priority inversion. Don't use semaphores for mutual exclusion.

sub_mechanisms.name: direct_to_task_notifications
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-task 32-bit notification value. Lighter than semaphore (no queue object).
sub_mechanisms.why: FreeRTOS optimization. ~45% faster than semaphore, less RAM. Use when single task is signalled.

sub_mechanisms.name: event_group_bitset
sub_mechanisms.definition: 32-bit bitset. Tasks wait for combinations of bits. AND or OR semantics.
sub_mechanisms.why: Multiple-condition synchronisation. Wait for 'config loaded AND network ready'. More expressive than single semaphores.

sub_mechanisms.name: tickless_idle
sub_mechanisms.definition: Skip tick interrupts when no work due. MCU sleeps until next scheduled event.
sub_mechanisms.why: Major power saving. 1 kHz tick = ~30 μA constant; tickless lets MCU truly sleep. Standard for battery devices.

sub_mechanisms.name: software_timer
sub_mechanisms.definition: Timer in RTOS, callback executed in timer daemon task.
sub_mechanisms.why: Many timers from one hardware timer. Periodic + one-shot. Callback runs in task context (not ISR) → less restricted.

sub_mechanisms.name: FreeRTOS_heap_implementations
sub_mechanisms.definition: 5 heap schemes. heap_1 (simple), heap_2 (basic free), heap_3 (malloc), heap_4 (best-fit + coalesce), heap_5 (multi-region).
sub_mechanisms.why: Trade-offs: simplicity, performance, fragmentation. heap_4 most common. heap_1 for hard RT (no free). Choose deliberately.

derivation_rules.name: bitmask_priority_O_1_selection
derivation_rules.why: 32-bit priority bitmask + count-leading-zeros = one instruction. Linear search through priorities defeats RT predictability. Standard RTOS pattern.

derivation_rules.name: context_switch_overhead_bounds_critical_section_granularity
then: critical sections shorter than N have no benefit from preemption
derivation_rules.why: If preemption itself takes longer than the work, don't preempt. Tasks should yield voluntarily for fine-grained work. Architectural decision.

derivation_rules.name: direct_notifications_faster_than_semaphores
if: only one task waits on a signal
derivation_rules.why: Semaphore: queue object, list traversal. Notification: per-task bits, direct write. ~45% faster. Less RAM. FreeRTOS-specific optimization.

derivation_rules.name: tickless_idle_major_battery_savings
if: device is battery-powered + sleeps majority of time
derivation_rules.why: 1ms tick = wake every ms = no real sleep. Tickless: MCU truly sleeps, wakes on real event. nRF: 30μA → 3μA average. Critical for years-on-battery devices.

derivation_rules.name: heap_choice_balances_simplicity_features
if: embedded application has specific memory needs
derivation_rules.why: heap_1 (no free): hard RT, no fragmentation. heap_4 (general): coalesces frees. heap_5 (multi-region): non-contiguous RAM. Default heap_4 for most.
